scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario. I have a best friend, G, who I've known since kindergarten. We've been super close, practically like brothers. G and my sister have always had a "thing," but they never officially dated for a long time. Finally, when we were 17, they started dating, and everything was great for about a year. But then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and was really mad at him. He asked me not to tell my sister, but I did. After that, we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was really weird for me because G is such a big part of my life. Eventually, G invited me on his family's ski trip as a way to make amends. I went, and after that, I forgave him and let him back into my life because it felt weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry, and he even cried, which I've only seen once before. G and my sister broke up after she found out about the cheating, and they're still not speaking. My sister is upset with me for still being friends with G and doesn't understand why our 13-year friendship is so important to me. I know G made a huge mistake, and I still hate him for it, but I don't want to lose our friendship over this. I'm thinking that if my best friend cheated on their SO, I wouldn't end our friendship, so why should this be any different just because his SO is my sister? We're also going to the same college in the fall, which is in a different state than where my sister is going. So, maybe this whole situation won't even be a big deal once we're living apart. Am I being an asshole here? I need to figure out if I'm handling this the right way or not. Let me break it down. First, I need to consider the dynamics of the relationships involved. G is my best friend, someone I've known for 13 years. My sister is my twin, so our relationship is very close. G and my sister had a history of being close, and they finally started dating. The cheating happened, which is a serious issue. I found out and was angry, and so was my sister when I told her. We had a period of not talking, which was really hard for me because G is such a significant person in my life. Then, G made an effort to make amends by inviting me on his family's ski trip. I accepted, and after that, I forgave him. I can see that he's genuinely sorry, which probably influenced my decision to forgive him. We're planning to go to the same college, which might mean that this situation will become less of a big deal as we move on with our lives. On the other hand, my sister is upset with me for still being friends with G. She doesn't understand why our friendship is so important to me, and she's making me feel bad about it. I think she expects me to take her side entirely, but I can't completely cut off a friendship that's been so significant to me. I need to evaluate whether it's right or wrong for me to continue this friendship despite G's actions. Is it wrong to prioritize my friendship with G over my sister's feelings? Or is it reasonable to maintain the friendship because G has shown remorse and because the friendship is so important to me? I also need to consider the potential long-term effects of this decision. If I continue to be friends with G, will it cause ongoing tension with my sister? Or will the situation eventually resolve itself as we move on with our lives? Since we're going to different colleges, maybe the distance will help ease some of the tension. Another aspect to consider is the nature of forgiveness. I forgave G, which is a personal choice. Forgiveness doesn't mean forgetting or excusing the behavior, but it does mean moving past it. I still hate him for what he did, but I'm choosing to keep the friendship. Is that a fair choice, or is it unfair to my sister? I also need to think about the boundaries in relationships. My sister might feel that I'm not taking her side, which could strain our relationship. On the other hand, I might feel that I'm being loyal to G, which is important to me. Balancing these loyalties is tricky. Additionally, I should consider the impact of G's actions on all parties involved. G cheated on my sister, which is a betrayal. He apologized, but the damage is done. My sister is hurt, and I'm caught in the middle. My decision to continue the friendship might be seen as supporting G over my sister, which could be hurtful to her. I also need to reflect on whether I'm being fair to myself. Am I holding onto this friendship because it's truly valuable, or am I doing it to avoid conflict or to make myself feel better? It's important to be honest with myself about my motivations. Furthermore, I should think about communication. Have I talked to my sister about why I'm choosing to keep the friendship? Have I explained my perspective to her? Clear communication might help her understand my position, even if she doesn't agree with it. I also need to consider the potential consequences of my decision. If I continue the friendship, will it lead to more problems down the line? Or will it allow everyone to move forward in a healthy way? It's possible that maintaining the friendship could help G grow and learn from his mistake, which might be beneficial for everyone involved. Another point to consider is the role of forgiveness in relationships. Forgiving someone doesn't mean that everything goes back to the way it was. It means that you're willing to move forward despite the hurt. I'm choosing to forgive G, but that doesn't mean I have to forget what he did. It's a personal choice that I'm making for myself. I also need to think about the bigger picture. In the long run, will this situation define my relationships with G and my sister, or will it be just a part of our history that we can move past? In summary, I need to evaluate whether continuing the friendship with G is the right choice, considering the hurt it has caused my sister, the importance of the friendship to me, the potential for growth and healing, and the long-term implications of my decision.
